review_notes: I read the whole file and Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean and Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean for `reparam` and `Homotopy.reparam`. I grepped Mathlib for existing helpers that turn an equality with a reparametrization into a homotopy and found none. The other repeated pieces are short: the four Quotient lemmas `refl_trans`, `trans_refl`, `trans_symm` and `symm_trans`, the `Quotient.sound ⟨...⟩` lines in the Groupoid instance, and the `split_ifs <;> constructor <;> linarith` proofs of the `*_mem_I` lemmas. I judged these routine or thin and did not report them. The finding below is moderate in strength because the helper is small. I have not compiled the proposed lemma.

findings.declaration: Path.Homotopy.transRefl and Path.Homotopy.transAssoc (with their reparametrization packages)
findings.problem: `transRefl` and `transAssoc` repeat the same construction. Each one (1) builds `Homotopy.reparam p f hf h0 h1 : Homotopy p (p.reparam f ..)`, (2) casts its right endpoint along the proved equation `q = p.reparam f ..` (`trans_refl_reparam` or `trans_assoc_reparam`), and (3) takes `.symm`. Each repeats the whole reparametrization package: the lambda `fun t => ⟨aux t, aux_mem_I t⟩`, `(by fun_prop)`, and `Subtype.ext aux_zero`/`Subtype.ext aux_one`. That package is written out twice in the equation lemma statement and again in the homotopy definition. So the proof pattern 'a path equal to a reparametrization of p is homotopic to p' sits inline in two places, and any change to the reparam API has to be made in both.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one generic constructor in `Path.Homotopy`, next to `Homotopy.reparam` (or at the start of this section):

```lean
/-- If `q` equals a reparametrization of `p` then `q` is homotopic to `p`. -/
def ofEqReparam {p q : Path x₀ x₁} (f : I → I) (hf : Continuous f) (hf₀ : f 0 = 0) (hf₁ : f 1 = 1)
    (h : q = p.reparam f hf hf₀ hf₁) : Homotopy q p :=
  ((Homotopy.reparam p f hf hf₀ hf₁).cast rfl h.symm).symm
```

The proof is exactly the existing cast-and-symm block. `h.symm : p.reparam f .. = q` has the type `cast` needs for the right endpoint, and the left endpoint is `rfl`.

Then rewrite the two uses under their current hypotheses:

```lean
def transRefl (p : Path x₀ x₁) : Homotopy (p.trans (Path.refl x₁)) p :=
  ofEqReparam _ (by fun_prop) (Subtype.ext transReflReparamAux_zero)
    (Subtype.ext transReflReparamAux_one) (trans_refl_reparam p)

def transAssoc {x₀ x₁ x₂ x₃ : X} (p : Path x₀ x₁) (q : Path x₁ x₂) (r : Path x₂ x₃) :
    Homotopy ((p.trans q).trans r) (p.trans (q.trans r)) :=
  ofEqReparam _ (by fun_prop) (Subtype.ext transAssocReparamAux_zero)
    (Subtype.ext transAssocReparamAux_one) (trans_assoc_reparam p q r)
```

The function argument `f` can be left as `_` because unification with `h` fixes it. If it does not elaborate, pass it explicitly. Optionally, state the two `*_reparam` lemmas through one named `def` for `f`, so that the lambda is written once per case instead of in the lemma, the homotopy and the helper arguments.
findings.benefit: `transRefl` and `transAssoc` shrink from five-line cast-and-symm terms to short statements of what is being used. The cast/symm argument is explained and checked once. Future changes to `Path.reparam` or `Homotopy.cast` need to be made in one place. Any further reparametrization-based homotopies, such as for `Path.trans` associativity variants, can reuse the helper.
